- **The handoff preserves human approval.**

content.body:
## Overview

A command that acts on the checkout it runs in behaves differently depending on which checkout that is, and nothing in the skill records which one a call site intends. Declaring the checkout per command and per procedure makes that intent machine-checkable, in the same way [#1457](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1457) made a worktree's placement checkable.

## Problem

- **A command's working directory decides what it changes, and only prose says which one.**
  `Merge Remote Branch` merges into the current worktree's branch. Run from a unit's worktree instead of an epic base's, it merges a long-lived branch into a task branch. The operations that call it name the worktree in prose, so the intent exists; nothing verifies a call site carries it.
- **An input a command cannot express goes unchecked.**
  `Merge Remote Branch` declares "Destination worktree" among its inputs while its command line has no way to name one, because the directory is the input. A caller that omits it produces no error anywhere.
- **The defect this generalises was live.**
  `Merge Task Pull Requests` ran `Update Epic Base` with no checkout named at all, and `Update Epic Base` declared an epic-base worktree nothing produced, as [#1454](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1454) recorded. Two read-only walks and the structure check both passed over it, and over the second instance [#1456](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1456) found.
- **The surface is 15 commands, not the wider one first estimated.**
  Of 95 `gh` blocks, 91 name `<owner>/<repo>` explicitly and the rest are examples or need no repository, so `gh` does not depend on the working directory here. The exposure is the non-worktree git family: `git merge`, `git push`, `git fetch`, `git rev-parse`, `git status`.

## Proposal

- **Name the checkouts once.**
  A closed vocabulary in the entry point's Conventions, beside Repository and Scripts: `project`, `epic base`, `unit`, `engineering`.
- **A command declares what it acts on.**
  A line beside Inputs, `**Acts on:** the checkout it runs in`, carried by every command whose behaviour depends on the working directory.
- **A procedure declares where it runs.**
  A line under the opening paragraph, `**Runs in:** the <name> checkout`, on each mode and protocol, and on a procedure subsection whose context differs from its file's. Deliver mode runs in `project` and its Run Delivery Session subsection in `unit`, which is the difference the original defect turned on.
- **A call site names the checkout.**
  Each call to a declaring command names one from the vocabulary, and a call naming a checkout other than its procedure's own passes it explicitly.
- **A test enforces the four above.**
  The citation graph the suite already walks supplies the call sites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Every command declaring that it acts on the checkout it runs in has each of its call sites naming a checkout from the vocabulary, verified by a test under `skills/work-planner/test/`.
- [x] **AC2.** Every mode and protocol, and every procedure subsection whose context differs from its file's, declares the checkout it runs in, verified by that same test.
- [x] **AC3.** A call naming a checkout other than its procedure's declared one passes that checkout among its named inputs, verified by that same test.
- [x] **AC4.** The test fails against the corpus at `27ea98734`, naming the `Update Epic Base` call that carried no checkout, verified by running it at that revision.

## Open Questions

- Do artifact operations declare a context of their own, or inherit every caller's and fail only on a conflict? Inheriting keeps the declaration count low and makes the check a graph walk rather than a per-file assertion.
- Does `project` need to distinguish the main working tree from any linked worktree, now that [#1456](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1456) anchors worktree paths to the former?

## Overview

An epic's or initiative's priority is a number in its board's Priority field. Board Queue reads that field and no label, and the `priority:` labels are gone.

## Problem

- **Priority has two homes.**
  Board Queue ranks by `priority: <n>` labels, through its [`RANK` pattern](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/scripts/board-queue.py#L33). Board 17's Priority field is a single-select of High, Medium and Low that nothing reads.
- **Labels that look like priorities don't rank.**
  workflow-server carries `priority: highest`, `high`, `medium`, `low` and `lowest`. Board Queue reads only numbered labels, so those issues have no priority.
- **The field can't hold a rank.**
  Three options can't express the numbered sets Board Queue runs, where the highest number runs together and the next waits in Ready.
- **Planning writes labels.**
  Plan mode [saves each confirmed number](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L72) as the epic's priority label.

## Proposal

- **Priority is a Number field.**
  Every theme board, and the Initiative template, has a Number field named Priority in place of the single-select. A larger number runs first. An empty value means no priority, and that epic never starts.
- **Board Queue reads the field.**
  `board-queue.py`, and every other script and rule that reads or sets a priority, use the board item's Priority field. No script or rule names a priority label.
- **Numbered labels move across, then every priority label goes.**
  Each open issue's `priority: <n>` becomes its board item's Priority value, unchanged. Word labels move nothing across.
- **Order of change.**
  The field values are set before the skill change merges. The labels are deleted only once prosiform's workspace pins a skill that reads the field, so every queue always has one source.

## Problem

- **The Links rules assume a reader who chooses.**

- **No rule states the bootstrap, the operators or the budget.**
  The shared guidelines name neither `pf`, nor the `⇉`, `⫽` and `¬` operators, nor a bundle's output budget.

## Proposal

- **The guidelines state the prosiform rules.**
  - A skill used through prosiform bootstraps from its entry point by running `pf` and following it.

## Overview

Work Planner's links carry the meaning prosiform gives them. Each names the section its reader needs, prose that only names another mode is plain text, a sub-agent hand-off dispatches the procedure the sub-agent follows, and material a step reads only in some cases is deferred. A mode's bundle then holds its own procedure and the sections it reaches, never another mode's.

## Problem

- **Links name whole files.**
  245 of Work Planner's 1075 internal links at [785a5ee8c](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner) name a whole file whose content carries sections, and prosiform compiles each whole file it reaches.
- **Modes link modes whole.**
  - [Plan Mode's Prerequisites](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L11-L27) link Propose Mode and Sync Mode;
  - [Deliver Mode's](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/deliver-mode.md#L11-L30) link Advance Mode and Hoist Mode;
  - [Sync Mode's](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/sync-mode.md#L22) link Understand Mode.
- **A hand-off is a sentence.**
  [Deliver Mode](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/deliver-mode.md#L101-L105) passes Run Delivery Session to a sub-agent through prose, and [Sync Mode](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/sync-mode.md#L175) runs Understand Mode inline. No Work Planner link carries an operator.
- **Conditional reads compile unconditionally.**
  [Plan Mode](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L37) runs Propose Mode only when neither a proposal nor an initiative is named, and [its ninth step](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L109) runs Sync Mode only once work has landed; both compile into every Plan bundle.

## Proposal

- **Each link names its section.**
  A whole-file link stays only where its target carries no heading below its title.
- **A mode named in passing is plain text.**
  Prose that attributes a behaviour to another mode names it without a link, so nothing compiles.
- **A step running another mode or a sub-agent dispatches it.**
  The step links the procedure with `⇉`, or `⫽` for a set run together, and prosiform publishes that procedure as a bundle of its own.
- **A conditional read is deferred.**
  A step that reads material only in some cases links it with `¬`, and the case stands in the step.
- **Prerequisites carry what the mode always reads.**
  A file a mode reaches only through a dispatch or a deferral leaves its Prerequisites.

content.body:
## Overview

Work Planner is used through prosiform. Its entry point tells the reader to select a mode, run `pf` on it and follow its bundle, every mode compiles within the default output budget with no warning and against stubs of its artifacts and protocols, and each mode's bundle size is compared against a fixed baseline revision. Once the skill's files conform, the shared skill-file check gains its prosiform findings, so a later change that breaks a prosiform rule in any skill it runs over draws a finding.

## Problem

- **No mode is an entry.**
  No Work Planner document declares prosiform, so no mode compiles on its own, and compiling [SKILL.md](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/SKILL.md#L19-L67) yields a 405673-byte bundle carrying every mode.
- **A mode is compiled only with everything it links.**
  A mode's own prose cannot be compiled apart from its artifacts and protocols, so a fault in one surfaces in every mode that reaches it.
- **Five modes overflow the default budget.**
  At [785a5ee8c](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner): Deliver 353717 bytes, Plan 328950, Advance 314874, Standup 273929 and Sync 264276, against 262144.
- **Nothing judges a unit's grain.**
  Whether a protocol, an artifact, or a procedure, operation, command or field within one is cut at the size its readers need is unmeasured, so a bundle carries content no step uses and a capability spreads across units, and a later change has no standard to be held to.
- **Nothing fixes what a change costs.**
  No record holds each mode's bundle size, so a change that grows a bundle is seen only when it crosses the budget.
- **The check reads resolution only.**
  The [shared skill-file check](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1025-L1029) confirms that a link resolves; a whole-file link to a file with sections, a mode linking another mode whole, and a mode that overflows the budget all pass.

## Proposal

- **SKILL.md routes to a mode.**
  The entry point is read, not compiled. Its Modes list selects a mode, and its instruction is to run `pf` on the selected mode file and follow that bundle. Each mode is an entry; SKILL.md is none.
- **The grain is reviewed first.**
  Before any mode is fitted to the budget, each protocol and artifact, and each procedure, operation, command and field section it holds, is measured for its share of each mode's bundle, its reach across modes, its dead weight in bundles whose steps do not use it, and its cohesion against the modes, protocols and artifacts layering. Each unit takes a verdict of keep, split, merge or move; the planning record holds the report, and each confirmed change becomes a row ahead of the budget fit. The measures, thresholds and verdict rules become Work Planner's grain rubric, which Revise Mode applies to every new or changed protocol and artifact.
- **Each mode fits its bundle.**
  A mode still over the budget once its links carry prosiform's meaning first hands each step a sub-agent runs to a `⇉` link compiled into its own bundle, then is cut to its own procedure, moving a section only some steps use to a file of its own.
- **Each mode compiles against stubs.**
  Each mode declares a `test` preset whose `subst` pairs replace the artifacts and protocols it links with stubs, so the mode's own prose compiles and is checked apart from theirs. The skill's test suite compiles every mode with that preset.
- **One comparison fixes the cost.**
  Each mode's bundle at the settled revision is compared with its bundle at the baseline revision, compiled by one prosiform version on both.
- **The check enforces the prosiform rules over every skill it runs over.**
  It reports a whole-file link to a target with sections, a mode or protocol reaching a mode file without an operator, and a mode whose compilation crosses the budget or warns. A missing or mismatched `pf` is a finding, never a skip.
- **The findings land after the skill conforms.**
  The check gains them last, so no branch carries a finding against the skill's own files.

| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform-skills/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1-i16-work-planner-repository/e07/w03.md) | Every mode compiled within budget | AC2 | W02 | | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A session given a Work Planner request selects a mode from the entry point, runs `pf` on that mode and follows its bundle, as a walk of a representative request from the entry point records.
- [ ] **AC2.** Every Work Planner mode on `main` compiles under the pinned `pf` within its default output budget with no warning, as each mode's compile recorded in the planning record shows.
- [ ] **AC3.** No Work Planner mode's bundle is larger than at the baseline revision the planning record fixes, as the bundle-size comparison records using one prosiform version on both revisions.
- [ ] **AC4.** The shared skill-file check reports a link naming no heading where its target carries one below its title, and none where the target carries no such heading, as `python3 -m unittest discover -s test` run from the repository root shows against a specimen skill carrying each.
- [ ] **AC5.** The shared skill-file check reports a mode or protocol file that reaches a mode file through a link carrying no operator, as `python3 -m unittest discover -s test` shows against a specimen skill carrying that link and one carrying a dispatch.

content.body:
## Overview

Four corrections to the work-planner skill. A hot-fix names its target branch, which may be any long-lived branch outside the initiative, epic and task branch structure, such as `workspace`. A hot-fix reaches Ready only once its issue is in the hot-fix format. Every delivery unit fixes the technical debt it finds in its own pull request, with no deferred-debt epic. And a rewritten issue body keeps no copy of the former one.

Target: `workspace`

## Problem

- **A hot-fix can only fix the default branch.** The hot-fix definition, branch and delivering-pull-request rules all read the repository's default branch.
  - A defect on another long-lived branch, such as workflow-server's `workspace`, cannot be a hot-fix.
  - Delivered as one, it would be cut from and merged into `main`.
- **Debt is parked behind all other work.** Deliver's debt step defers a non-trivial item to the initiative's deferred-debt epic, its last epic.
  - The clear-up then waits until every other epic of the initiative has delivered.
  - The owner's standing rule is the opposite: debt a delivery finds is fixed in that delivery.
- **Two debt rules for one decision.** A hot-fix unit already fixes all its debt in its own pull request, while an epic unit sorts it into Blocking, Trivial and Non-trivial.
  - The classification exists only to choose between fixing and deferring.

## Proposal

- **Hot-fix definition.** A hot-fix fixes a defect in one long-lived branch outside the initiative, epic and task branch structure.
  - The rule lives in the hot-fix body's Definition.
- **Target line.** A hot-fix body carries a `Target:` line naming that branch.
  - Hoist proposes the repository's default branch and the user confirms the target with the placement.
  - The hot-fix body's fields state the line once; the hot-fix entity's Branch and Delivering Pull Request read it.
- **Cut from and merged into the target.** A hot-fix's branch is cut from its target, and its delivering pull request has the target as its base.
  - The plan names the target in the unit line, so no default-branch lookup remains.
  - The scripts read the target from the body through the hot-fix module alone.
- **Ready only once formatted.** A hot-fix reaches Ready only after its issue carries the hot-fix title, labels and body.
  - Hoist places it in Backlog, rewrites it, then sets the status Board Status gives an open hot-fix.
  - The board queue moves an open hot-fix that fails the hot-fix format to Backlog.
- **One debt rule for every unit.** A unit fixes every debt item its validation finds on its task branch, so its open pull request carries the fix before it merges.
  - The rule has one home, which Deliver's debt step and the hot-fix Debt field link.
- **No classification and no deferred-debt epic.** The Blocking, Trivial and Non-trivial classes are removed with the deferral they chose between.
  - The initiative body's Deferred Debt field, its criterion and its tests are removed.
  - An open epic titled `Deferred Debt` is an ordinary epic of its initiative.
- **Debt beyond the unit's code.**
  Debt in code outside the unit's change is an arising issue, created and hoisted by Deliver's arising-issues step.

- **Rewrites keep no copy.** A rewritten issue body is saved with no comment preserving the former body.
  - Placement's rewrite saves the new body alone, and placement has no Original Body field.

- **Draft until reviewed.** A hot-fix pull request opens as a draft and is marked ready for review only once its review cycle leaves no blocking finding.
  - A draft is never a merge candidate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The hot-fix Definition admits any long-lived branch outside the initiative, epic and task branch structure, read in the hot-fix body artifact.
- [ ] **AC2.** Every hot-fix body names its target in one `Target:` line that hoist confirms, checked by the format script's tests.
- [ ] **AC3.** A hot-fix unit's branch is cut from its target and only a pull request into its target delivers it, checked by the hot-fix module's tests.
- [ ] **AC4.** No skill file or script reads a repository's default branch to deliver a hot-fix, checked by a search of the skill.
- [ ] **AC5.** The rule that a unit fixes its debt in its own pull request is stated in one artifact that Deliver mode and the hot-fix Debt field link, checked by a search of the skill.
- [ ] **AC6.** No skill file, script or test names a deferred-debt epic or a Non-trivial deferral, checked by a search of the skill.
- [ ] **AC7.** No hot-fix stands Ready or In Progress before its title, labels and body meet the hot-fix format, read in the hot-fix entity artifact and checked by the board-queue tests.
- [ ] **AC8.** No skill file or test posts or preserves a former issue body when a body is rewritten, checked by a search of the skill.
- [ ] **AC9.** A hot-fix pull request opens as a draft and is marked ready only once its review cycle leaves no blocking finding, and no draft is a merge candidate, checked by the delivery-plan script's tests.
- [ ] **AC10.** The skill's tests and skill-file check pass, checked by Run Tests and Check Skill Files.

## References

- **R1.** [Hot-fix Body](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/12cf5b38666f827f5ec00e9f2aa468b0bfb4150d/skills/work-planner/artifacts/hotfix-body.md#definition) — the definition this issue widens.
- **R2.** [Hot-fix](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/12cf5b38666f827f5ec00e9f2aa468b0bfb4150d/skills/work-planner/artifacts/hotfix.md#branch) — the branch and delivering-pull-request rules that read the target.
- **R3.** [Deliver debt step](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/12cf5b38666f827f5ec00e9f2aa468b0bfb4150d/skills/work-planner/modes/deliver-mode.md) — the classification and deferral this issue removes.

content.body:
## Overview

A project that requires no criterion of its epics should be able to say so with an empty declaration, or none, and have the check hold its epics to nothing. Today that statement is reported as an error on every epic checked.

Target: `workspace`

## Problem

- **An empty declaration is reported as a fault.**
  [`required_criteria`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/42e67e0044b5023efd9c57a89628a88ee459df0c/skills/work-planner/scripts/format.py#L341-L370) returns the criteria unevaluable for a missing `config/required-criteria.json`, an empty file and an empty array alike, so `format.py` prints `required criteria unevaluable: …` for every epic of such a project.
- **The guide states the same rule.**
  The [Required Criteria](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/42e67e0044b5023efd9c57a89628a88ee459df0c/skills/work-planner/artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#required-criteria) bullet "An absent statement is unevaluable" groups a missing or empty file and an empty array with unreadable JSON.
- **A project with nothing to require has no clean way to state it.**
  It must either live with the finding or declare a criterion that is not true of it. prosiform, which has no recurring criterion, hit this when adopting the declaration.

## Proposal

- **Nothing declared requires nothing.**
  A missing or empty file at the evaluated commit, or an empty array, yields no required criterion and no finding.
- **Only an unreadable statement is unevaluable.**
  A revision resolving to no commit, unreadable JSON, a value other than an array, or an entry lacking a field stays unevaluable, reported as it is now.

content.body:
## Overview

Deliver mode merges each task pull request into its epic base without review, and the skill says so. An agent harness can still refuse that merge on its own judgement, and the skill has no answer for it, so a delivery stalls and the user is asked to approve a merge the skill already authorizes.

Target: `workspace`

## Problem

- **A harness refusal is read as a GitHub refusal.**
  [Merge Task Pull Request](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/b1eb5351b97add7f5f74428abfdec142b35548e4/skills/work-planner/artifacts/pull-request.md#L150-L158) states that the epic base carries no review requirement and merges "without further confirmation". Its only refusal path updates the task branch and retries once, which suits a stale head. A refusal from the agent's own permission layer is not about the head, so the retry fails the same way and the pull request is left open "with the blocker reported".
- **Claude Code's auto-mode classifier refuses these merges.**
  The classifier blocks an agent merging a pull request it opened as `[Merge Without Review]`. It sees neither branch protection nor the skill, so it cannot tell an epic base, which needs no review, from `main`, which does. In prosiform delivery (m2ux/prosiform#511) the delivery session's merge was refused, the session handed the pull request back, and the orchestrating session asked the user to approve a merge the skill had already authorized.
- **The skill never states the permission Deliver needs.**
  [Dependencies](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/b1eb5351b97add7f5f74428abfdec142b35548e4/skills/work-planner/SKILL.md#dependencies) lists `gh`, the sandbox and sub-agents. It does not say that the harness must let a session merge into an epic base, so nothing checks for this before units are dispatched, and every refused merge reaches the user.

## Proposal

- **Deliver names the harness permission it needs.**
  The skill states that a delivery session must be able to merge a task pull request into an epic base (`iNN/eNN/main`) unprompted, while merges into the default branch stay with a person. It gives the Claude Code form: an `autoMode.allow` rule and an `autoMode.environment` entry in user settings, both keeping `$defaults`.
- **Deliver checks for it before dispatching.**
  Before the first unit is dispatched, Deliver confirms that the permission is in place. If it is missing, the run reports exactly which setting is absent, so no session finds out at its merge.
- **A harness refusal is its own outcome.**
  Merge Delivery Pull Request tells a permission-layer refusal apart from a GitHub one. A permission refusal on a base with no review requirement is neither a handoff for approval nor a branch blocker. The session returns the pull request as ready and verified, naming the refusal. The orchestrating session merges it, or reports the missing permission, and does not ask the user to approve it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** The skill states the permission Deliver needs to merge task pull requests into an epic base, with the Claude Code `autoMode` settings that grant it and the default branch left with a person.
- [x] **AC2.** Deliver checks for that permission before dispatching its first unit, and reports the missing setting when it is absent.
- [x] **AC3.** Merge Delivery Pull Request distinguishes a permission-layer refusal from a GitHub refusal. On a base with no review requirement, the permission refusal returns to the orchestrating session for merge, never to the user for approval.

content.body:
## Overview

Every session writes its planning record into one shared engineering worktree. The skill tells each session to commit only its own folder, so another session's work is never swept along. The user's preference is the opposite. Any commit on engineering may include unrelated work, and each commit sweeps everything uncommitted or unpushed in the worktree, idempotently. That way no session's record is left stranded.

Target: `workspace`

## Problem

- **A folder-scoped commit leaves other sessions' work unpublished.**
  [Commit Planning Record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/f8b2812cf/skills/work-planner/artifacts/planning-record.md#commit-planning-record) stages and commits one folder with `git commit -- <folder>`, "so a concurrent session's staged work cannot ride along". A session that writes a file and then stops, fails or is interrupted before its own commit leaves that file uncommitted. Nothing else ever commits it, so the record's links stay broken.
- **Design edits fall outside any planning folder.**
  Delivery sessions also commit `design.md` on engineering. The folder rule says nothing about that file, so each brief has to restate how to commit it. A session that commits its folder alone can leave an earlier design edit unpushed.
- **The isolation it buys is not wanted.**
  [Shared Worktree](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/f8b2812cf/skills/work-planner/artifacts/planning-record.md#shared-worktree) has a session confirm that its own files landed in its own commit. Planning records are working notes pushed straight to the branch. In prosiform delivery (I08 and I09, 2026-11-02), one integration session's push published another session's unpushed `design.md` commit. That was the right outcome, but it ran against the rule as written.

## Proposal

- **A commit on engineering sweeps the worktree.**
  Commit Planning Record runs `git add -A` in the engineering worktree and commits if anything is staged. Then it runs `git fetch origin engineering && git rebase origin/engineering` and pushes. Run twice with nothing new, it does nothing, so any session can run it at any time.
- **Shared Worktree states the sweep.**
  The field says a commit may carry other sessions' work, and that a session confirms only that its own files are on `origin/engineering` after the push, not that they sit in a commit of their own.
- **One operation covers the record and the design.**
  The same sweep commits a `design.md` amendment, so briefs and modes link the operation and do not restate a path-scoped command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Commit Planning Record stages everything in the engineering worktree, commits only when something is staged, rebases on `origin/engineering` and pushes, so a second run with no new changes leaves the branch unchanged.
- [x] **AC2.** Shared Worktree states that a commit on engineering may include other sessions' uncommitted or unpushed work, and that a session confirms its own files reached `origin/engineering`.
- [x] **AC3.** No mode, protocol or artifact tells a session to limit an engineering commit to its own paths.

content.body:
## Overview

The work-planner skill gains SOLID guidelines fitted to its architecture, and the whole skill is audited and fixed against them in workflow-server before the skill's extraction is cut. Artifact and protocol files own their subjects, callable operations and command specifications; links select those capabilities and their required context. Each rule has one owning file or script module, and no general file names a specific kind of work, so the skill moves to prosiform-skills already separated.

## Problem

- **No separation grain is defined.** The guidelines define an artifact as one shape and a protocol as one change. They say nothing of how files encapsulate, extend or depend on one another.
  - Open–closed is stated only for the issue-body family: "the common file names no kind".
- **General files enumerate kinds of work.** The delivery plan, Deliver mode, pull request, board queue and Task Merge each name hot-fixes and branch on them.
  - Adding a kind means editing every general file again.
- **Scripts branch on kinds inline.**
  The delivery and board-queue scripts run hot-fix paths beside the epic paths.
- **Fields carry hidden behavior.**
  Board Delivery’s Status Changes computes status and membership decisions from delivery evidence and restricts permitted writes inside a field definition. Similar sections can conceal derivation or execution behind declarative wording.
- **Required reads are circular and broad.**
  A prerequisite cycle spans Board Delivery, Board Queue, Delivery Branches, Delivery Plan and related artifact modules. Whole-file imports pull unrelated command bodies into Standup and Understand before their selected operations run.
- **Retained preparation can reach creation.**
  Unit Dispatch accepts retained preparations but its session-preparation step calls Create Task Worktree unconditionally. A capacity-only resume can attempt to recreate the recorded branch and checkout.
- **Policy contexts can disagree.**
  Advance decision recording, backlog cascades, diagram sizing and hot-fix finding scope have competing readings. An ownership move alone cannot settle which inputs and outcomes a rule governs.
- **No map of the breaches.**
  Nobody has audited the whole skill, so the remaining breaches and their owning homes are unknown.

## Proposal

- **Files own subjects and capabilities.** An artifact or protocol file owns one subject or coordinated change, and callers select its operations or command specifications by link.
  - Commands precedes Fields and owns the enriched invocation and explicit I/O contract. Callers Run command specifications directly where no substantive procedure is needed.
  - Fields are the file's state and public shape. Nested calls keep selections, conditions and continuation without repeating I/O inventories.
  - In-text links select required context at its point of use, with common context separated from context selected by a particular operation.
- **SOLID guidelines first.** The first task adds a SOLID section to the skill's guidelines.
  - Single responsibility: one reason to change per file.
  - Open–closed: a new kind is a new file, and general files name no kind.
  - Liskov substitution: every kind fills an interface operation with the same contract.
  - Interface segregation: small callable capabilities, common prerequisites justified for every entry they govern, and conditional context reached at its point of use.
  - Dependency inversion: general files never link down to a kind, and kinds are listed in one registry.
  - Each file-type section links that section rather than restating it.
  - Define the required-before-use context graph separately from execution calls and ordinary field references. Its edges name their entry condition, required content and reason; the graph is acyclic. A selected link sets the reading boundary; linked modes execute only at explicit calls. Ordinary cross-reference cycles do not imply before-use ordering cycles.
  - Fields define shapes and invariants; operations own derivation, execution, refusals and continuation. The audit distinguishes legitimate conditional constraints from hidden transformations.
- **Audit against the guidelines.** The second task reviews every artifact, mode, protocol and script against the guidelines' audit questions.
  - It records each breach in the planning record with its file, the guideline it breaks and the home that owns it. Every Fields section is classified; Board Delivery’s Status Changes is the confirmed starting finding. Candidates record the supplied evidence, produced decision, owning subject and disposition.
  - Classify every prerequisite edge by source section, target boundary, entry condition and necessity. Record required common context, context selected by a call, field definitions read at use and redundant preloads. Trace Standup, Revise and Understand from stable source revisions, including their consumer-specific context.
- **Fix rows from the audit.**
  Each fix row groups the files of one concern the audit names and carries its observing regressions; parallel rows never edit the same file.
- **Tasks name every file.**
  A task row may change many files. Its work item declares each one, and the dependency check and delivery survey group, join and route rows by any file they share.
- **Kind registration.**
  The entry point names each kind's artifact and the interface operations it supplies, and one script registry, `scripts/kinds.py`, maps each kind to its module. General prose and scripts reach a kind only through them; the hot-fix artifacts and module supply the operations.
- **Shared executable rules.**
  Title tag parsing lives in `scripts/board.py`, completion and issue identity in `scripts/sync.py`, and priority-label interpretation in the `scripts/priority.py` that #1631 delivers.
- **Kind review operation.**
  The Kind interface carries the review rule a kind applies: which record fields make a review current and the finding fault it adds. Hot-fix supplies today's rule, and agent_review.py asks the selected kind.
- **One definition per pattern.**
  The title-tag and pull-request home patterns are each defined once, in the module both sync.py and board.py can import, and the template test states its own import path.
- **Bounded prerequisite reads.** Apply the reviewed edge dispositions to remove circular and unrelated preload requirements while retaining necessary common context, selected command contracts, authorization and evidence gates. Keep each rule at its owning subject; a visited-set workaround or an instruction to ignore an import does not settle an ownership or read-boundary defect.
  - Fixed routes supply complete, untruncated common and selected-operation context before use. Paired fresh-context trials use pinned source and executable captured fixtures; each trial records actual reads, omissions, unrelated content and prerequisite reuse.
- **Board Status artifact.** A new `board-status.md` owns the proposed status-change shape and the operations that derive and validate that change. Board Delivery gathers evidence, applies changes and confirms saved state. Board Queue retains priority/readiness decisions; lifecycle rules stay with their owning subjects.
  - The audit separately checks for a shared ordered sequence changing several artifacts. A lifecycle protocol requires that concrete sequence and its callers, reconciled with Issue Delivery and Issue Closure; decision rules alone remain with their owning artifacts.
  - The artifact, Board Delivery and Hot-fix consumer changes share one pull request so moved contracts, caller links and `○`, `●`, `ƒ` roles remain valid together. Existing status, membership, assignee, review-evidence and write-scope behavior is preserved.
- **Candidate detection and regression evidence.** Checker fixtures include the actual Status Changes text, structurally different hidden-transform examples and valid conditional field constraints. Diagnostics identify file, heading, evidence and candidate operation/owner; semantic classification is confirmed in the audit.
  - Extracted behavior and prerequisite fixes carry regression coverage in their own pull requests. The final checker task adds reusable candidate detection and prerequisite diagnostics with positive/negative fixtures; wording keywords alone do not establish a violation.
  - Cycle diagnostics name source/target sections and a closed witness path. Scope diagnostics are conservative review candidates unless a declared context contract proves the mismatch. Valid conditional prerequisites, ordinary definition cycles and intentional execution retries are controls.
- **Verified retained-preparation route.** After the separation diagnostics are available, reconcile Unit Dispatch with the existing automatic-dispatch correction in #1631 and [PR #1645](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1645). Creation records the preparation head; a retained preparation selects the owning read-only worktree validation, using the recorded checkout identity and current hold/start evidence. Keep that identity contract and its executable validation in Delivery Branches, with selection and continuation in Unit Dispatch.
  - Verify the separated route with the completed prerequisite diagnostics and capacity-wait/resume fixtures. A mismatch retains the checkout and hold, blocks that unit, and starts no worker. Successful reuse reaches the existing start gate once; new work still follows creation.
  - Reuse the upstream implementation and observing tests. Defects in that implementation are corrected in its owning pull request; this task reconciles its protocol calls and verifies their composition with the separated skill.
- **Policy clarification decisions.** The audit includes the four inherited ambiguities in the [policy clarification plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/policy-clarifications.md). Each candidate has its exact context, current prose and observed behavior, recommended interpretation, owning contract and distinguishing scenarios.
  - Audit and proposed interpretations are authorized; each policy interpretation is confirmed before its fix is dispatched. Distinguish a wording conflict from different rules governing different contexts.
  - The ownership fixes apply confirmed interpretations and their observing regressions together, with one canonical rule and links from callers. Group fixes by concern into task rows that name every file they change before dispatch and reconcile shared files with the delivery-recovery plan.
  - Use the Style epic's field ledger and review evidence as the starting inventory, then refresh against its delivered revision; a resolved presentation or field-boundary issue is not repeated as an open defect.
- **Behaviour.**
  Ownership-only fixes preserve outcomes. A confirmed policy clarification records its permitted outcome differences and observing scenarios before implementation; extraction regressions compare against that clarified baseline.

- **Backlog pause has its own delivery.**
  The audit records the selected cascade: all unfinished descendants move to Backlog and active work pauses with its initiative; completed descendants remain Done. The dedicated Backlog Pause plan owns the runtime implementation. This epic's ownership fixes retain the audited runtime baseline and consume the other confirmed policy decisions.

The style is the one the example skill under `.project/main/example` shows. That example is an older work-planner and serves as a structural style reference only: no content carries over from it. Command presentation follows the linked Graph Index example in R5. Context is selected through in-text links, and no prosiform metadata is added. ## Problem - **Steps are list items.** Every procedure is a numbered list with bold leads, so a step has no heading to link and no place for its own detail. - **Command contracts are implicit.** Invocations lack contextual input and output links, while usage details and repeated parameter inventories obscure their execution contract. - **Inputs and outputs lack explicit roles.** Command specifications do not consistently link every consumed or provided value to its owning Field, leaving part of the execution contract implied. - **SKILL.md carries the rules.** The rules and conventions that bind every mode, and the deployment values, sit in SKILL.md and the guidelines rather than in files of their own. - **The style model describes the installed layout.** The current declarations and checks do not define the proposed heading-based steps, linked contracts and HTML command blocks. ## Proposal - **Per-skill style model.** The skill's own guidelines, `structure.json` and `rules.json` state the new model, and the shared checker reads each skill's declared model. - The shared guidelines and every other skill keep their current shape. - Checker support is proven against specimen skills before document conversion. The final task adopts Work Planner's new guidelines and model declarations once every conversion is complete; the installed declarations govern the live checks until that adoption. - **Entry files.** SKILL.md keeps its opening, Modes and Dependencies. - `rules.md` holds the rules that bind every mode, `conventions.md` the conventions, and `configuration.md` the deployment values, each built from the live skill's own text. - **Steps as sub-sections.** Each step is a heading of its position and action. A step with multiple contained instruction or detail items bullets every item; a single item is plain text. - Calls use Run for a command, Apply for an artifact operation and Follow for a mode, protocol or child procedure. - Each mode and protocol opens with the preamble line that links Rules, Conventions and, for a mode, Outcomes. - **Named command specifications.** A `## Commands` section precedes Fields and holds each enriched invocation once. Its imperative preamble states the action and provides its linked output to the requester. Operations call commands with the necessary selections, conditions and continuations. Linked arguments establish their contracts without a repeated parameter list in prose. - Value-format and output examples appear on the owning Field's description line as `eg` with inline code. Structural templates keep their fences. Single-sentence conditions accompany the command preamble; multi-item command details follow the invocation. - Command and tool-access invocations use raw HTML `
…
` blocks, matching the specific R5 step. Contract-backed input names are bold Markdown links inside the block, using role-tagged `[**argument**](#argument-contract "○")`. Long shell invocations use backslash-newline continuations at token boundaries, grouping options with their values while preserving literal syntax and argument order. Shell quoting follows the value type: validated shell-safe numbers/identifiers and fixed safe literals are unquoted; variable paths, refs, free text and query expressions retain their required quoting. - Checker fixtures accept this HTML command form and its resolving argument links, and reject Markdown-fenced command invocations. The example supplies presentation only; its tool names, graph behavior, content and metadata are outside this migration. - **Inputs, outputs and contracts.** Each command links every consumed input and provided output to its owning `###` Field in contextual prose or the invocation. Nested operations do not repeat I/O contracts. Markdown link titles mark `"○"` for input, `"●"` for output and `"ƒ"` for a called command, operation, protocol or procedure. Results use Provide. `rules.md` defines the tags, and the guidelines require an independent completeness check against commands, calls, conditions and results. Performed-operation contract verification remains a future feature. - Fields define scalar or composite data objects and valid-state constraints. A single-use rule belongs with its caller; shared policy has one linked Guidance home. Artifact operations own shared procedures with meaningful decisions or processing. - In-text links select context at its use. ## Overview

An initiative sync changes the Done cell of only the rows whose epic it was given, so a run naming one just-merged epic keeps every other delivered epic's tick and reports those rows as left unchanged.

Target: `workspace`

## Problem

- **A missing epic reads as undelivered.**
  [`initiative_delivery`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9d71790c2668debbc03a2ba1d00509e8bea3bff6/skills/work-planner/scripts/sync.py#L296-L306) sets `delivered[epic] = bool(issue) and epics.get(int(issue[1]), False)`. A row whose issue is not among `--epics` falls back to `False`, and its Done cell is written empty.
- **The report does not flag the loss.**
  The only output is `note: <row id>: its id links no issue given by --epics`, an informational remark. The run still writes the body, and its output does not show that ticks are removed.
- **Observed in prosiform delivery (2026-11-02).**
  After one epic of a prosiform initiative merged into `main`, a `sync.py --fix` run naming only that epic cleared the Done ticks of six other delivered and closed epics. The body was published and later restored by hand.

## Proposal

- **An epic not given keeps its tick.**
  `initiative_delivery` changes only the rows whose epic issue is among `--epics`. Every other row's Done cell is left as it stands.
- **The report names what was not checked.**
  The note says that the row was left unchanged because its epic was not given, so a partial run reads as partial.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** An initiative synced with a subset of its epics keeps the Done cell of every row whose epic is not given, as a `sync.py --fix` run with one epic over a body with several ticked rows shows.
- [x] **AC2.** A row whose epic is not given is reported as left unchanged, as the same run's output shows.

## Overview

A hot-fix whose pull request awaits review should stand In Review, as any other work item does. The skill bars it from that column, so a hot-fix waiting on the user's approval sits In Progress, where the user does not look for work to review.

Target: `workspace`

## Problem

- **A hot-fix never stands In Review.**
  [Board Status](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/a5ff02d92/skills/work-planner/artifacts/hotfix.md#board-status) states "A hot-fix never stands In Review: one found there moves to In Progress", and `hotfix.py` returns In Progress for a hot-fix held In Review.
- **The board scripts enforce it.**
  `statuses.py` says only an initiative or an epic stands In Review, and `board-queue.py` moves a hot-fix's In Review back to In Progress. A hot-fix set In Review by hand returns to In Progress on the next Advance.
- **Observed on board 17.**
  F03 (#1586), F04 (#1608) and F05 (#1613) had ready, reviewed pull requests awaiting the user's approval, and all three stood In Progress.

## Proposal

- **A hot-fix awaiting review stands In Review.**
  An open hot-fix whose [delivering pull request](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/a5ff02d92/skills/work-planner/artifacts/hotfix.md#delivering-pull-request) is marked ready for review stands In Review. It stands In Progress while that pull request is a draft.

content.body:
## Overview

A board can be delivered by more than one session at once, each serving its own lane of task rows. Each row carries its lane as a bare index in the epic Work Breakdown table, Plan mode assigns it, and a Deliver run naming a lane takes its lane’s rows and unlaned rows. The epic lands before the skill’s extraction, so the skill moves with lanes.

## Problem

- **The live task table has no lane column.**
  Its Task, Description, Coverage, Depends on, Joins and Done cells contain no lane assignment.
- **Work-item declarations split the row’s plan.**
  The epic base’s Work Item artifact defines a separate Lane declaration, so the task table alone cannot show or supply a row’s lane.
- **Every session sees one queue.**
  The delivery survey offers available units by priority and dependencies, so two sessions on one board can select the same unit.
- **A label cannot carry it.**
  A label marks an issue, while task rows in one epic can belong to different lanes and have no task issue.

## Proposal

- **The task table owns the lane.**
  Its columns are `Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done`. Lane contains a bare decimal index such as `2`; an empty cell is unlaned.
- **A lane is an opaque board-wide index.**
  The same index names one lane across the theme board. Its cell contains the index alone.
- **The request names the run’s lane.**
  A Deliver request states its lane each time. A request naming none is offered only unlaned units.
- **A laned run also admits unlaned work.**
  A run is offered its lane’s units and unlaned units, ordered by priority. Hot-fix units are unlaned.
- **Plan mode writes the task cells.**
  It asks whether the initiative uses lanes, proposes each row’s index for confirmation and passes the confirmed values to Populate Epic Issue Body.
- **Joined rows share one lane.**
  Their Lane cells carry the same index or are all empty. The dependency check refuses a split unit, settled by changing a lane or unjoining.
- **Readers use the issue body.**
  Dependency checks, delivery and queue reporting use one task-table lane reader. Work-item files supply components and implementation plans.
- **Table operations preserve lanes.**
  Format validation checks bare indices, and normalization, reservation, release, linking and Done ticks preserve the Lane cell.
- **The queue reports unit lanes.**
  Board Queue reports each Ready unit’s lane from its existing issue snapshots, and Advance carries those report lines.

content.body:
## Overview

Work Planner leaves failed readiness and merge attempts in an explicit, verified state. Hot-fix review failure withdraws ready state, and epic integration follows the owning merge result without unintended retries or success assertions.

## Problem

- Hot-fix readiness can fail after marking a pull request ready, while the repair route promises draft state without an explicit restoring write and readback.
- Epic integration treats refusal generically although the owning merge operation distinguishes harness denial and GitHub refusal, and its final readback assumes a merge.
- The task merge command omits the verified head SHA, so a head moving between verification and the mutation can merge unverified content.
- The merge-permission field describes task-to-epic-base authorization while the shared operation handles further delivery targets.

## Proposal

Deliver Mode selects the existing draft command and confirms its result before hot-fix repair. Pull Request owns explicit merge outcomes and the permission boundary; Epic Integration consumes them with bounded retry and terminal handoff/refusal branches. One atomic unit changes the shared merge contract and its epic caller. The task merge mutation includes its verified head SHA; a mismatch supplies refusal evidence for fresh verification within the existing retry bound. Behavior is verified with ordered calls and terminal-result fixtures, including restoration failure and each refusal source.

## Work Breakdown

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1657) | Confirm draft state after failed hot-fix readiness | AC1, AC2, AC3 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | | | ✓ |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1658) | Explicit merge outcomes and permission boundaries | AC4, AC5, AC8 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | W03 | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1658) | Epic continuation follows the merge outcome | AC6, AC7 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | W02 | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** A hot-fix validation failure after a ready write selects draft restoration and confirms current draft state before repair, as ordered failure-route fixtures show.
- [x] **AC2.** A failed restoration or disagreeing readback produces an explicit unresolved discrepancy without claiming draft state or reaching merge/In Review, as negative fixtures show.
- [x] **AC3.** Passing hot-fix review and ready readback reaches normal merge exactly once, as a positive route fixture shows.
- [x] **AC4.** Merge Delivery Pull Request provides distinct confirmed-merge, human-handoff, harness-denial and GitHub-refusal outcomes with current head/target evidence, as contract and outcome fixtures show.
- [x] **AC5.** Merge Permission describes the existing authorization/capability boundary for each supported delivery target without authorizing protection bypass or widening harness permission, as source review against configured target requirements and permission-denial fixtures shows.
- [x] **AC6.** Epic integration terminates human handoff and harness denial without same-run retry or merged-success readback, as ordered negative fixtures show.
- [x] **AC7.** Epic integration retries GitHub refusal only within the existing bound after fresh verification, terminates repeated refusal, and confirms merged head/target/commit only after a confirmed merge, as route fixtures show.

- [x] **AC8.** The task merge mutation includes the verified head SHA and refuses a moved head without a success claim or unchecked retry, as captured-request and moving-head refusal fixtures show.

content.body:
## Overview

Plan Mode publishes a new epic for an existing initiative, saves its parent row with the created identity, and validates fresh saved context before delivery preparation.

## Problem

The [publication procedure](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/3223aee0e83766bf9ef5727662ce3626115a27ae/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L68-L85) places epic creation and identity replacement under the new-initiative branch. The existing-initiative route reaches validation without an explicit save of its new epic or the parent's new row. The ambiguity predates the style migration.

## Proposal

Initiative creation is conditional; epic publication and confirmed identity substitution serve both new and existing parents. Plan Mode owns the sequencing and calls the existing save/readback capabilities. Fresh issue identities and bodies supply format, goal and dependency validation. Failed saves stop downstream preparation with their evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
